newsitem.title: INDIA: India retains import curbs on consumer electronics.
newsitem.headline: India retains import curbs on consumer electronics.

text.p: India's Commerce Ministry, unveiling a new five-year trade policy, said on Monday that consumer electronics goods, watches and telephone instruments continued to remain under import restrictions.

"For the removal of doubt, it is hereby declared that consumer goods shall also include the following and shall not be imported except against a licence or in accordance with a public notice," it said in a handbook on the new policy. It listed consumer electronic goods, watches and telephone instruments.
The policy statement also listed cotton, woollen, silk, man-made and blended fabrics including cotton terry towels in the list of imports still under restrictions.
Wines, saffron and concentrates of alcoholic beverages were also still under restrictions, it added.
The government said it had removed import restrictions on 542 items which can now be imported freely or bought through freely-transferable special import licences.
The ministry said it would release the list of 542 items later on Monday.
